messages:
alex.nguyen: Hey team — escalation from a larger customer reporting streaming responses are suddenly much slower for first chunk (TTFB) since ~2026-03-12 02:05 UTC. Non-streaming (sync) calls are OK. p95/p99 for first chunk jumped ~800-1200ms. Need triage; customer sees impact on UX for chat streaming.

maria.perez: Thanks Alex. Do we have example request_ids or logs? Are they using our hosted API or dedicated? Any change in client side (proxies) noted?

alex.nguyen: They're hosted, high throughput. Customer provided two request_ids: req_0a1b2c3d and req_0f9e8d7c. They say it started shortly after our runtime roll last week. No customer-side proxy changes reported.

alex.nguyen: Repro steps I used locally (simple curl to mimic streaming):
```bash
# streaming (sse/chunked) emulation
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-x"
```
This shows the first chunk delay often much larger than non-streaming call: 50-100ms vs 900-1200ms in affected env.

jonathan.kirby: I rolled the runtime change that touched chunk coalescing and socket flush timing on 2026-03-11 23:40 UTC — PR #3421. The goal was to reduce number of small writes (perf) by coalescing small frames. Could be a regression for clients that rely on immediate flush. Link: https://git.internal/pr/3421

liz_sre: That sounds plausible. Coalescing reduces syscalls but increases head-of-line for first chunk. Two quick checks: confirm tcp_nodelay is still enabled on the worker side, and grab a few tcpdump traces to verify when bytes leave the server vs when they're processed. Also check kernel-level send buffer / Nagle interactions.

alex_nguyen: Pasted a small snippet from our streaming runtime logs for req_0a1b2c3d: 
```
[2026-03-12T02:05:12.123Z] stream.emit_chunk req=req_0a1b2c3d size=256 flush=false queued_ms=1028
[2026-03-12T02:05:12.123Z] stream.kv_cache_hit req=req_0a1b2c3d
[2026-03-12T02:05:12.124Z] connection.write req=req_0a1b2c3d bytes=256 flushed=false
```
The queued_ms value looks like the runtime delaying flush.

maria.perez: Can we confirm this is coalescing-induced and not network queueing? Alex, can you repro by forcing a socket flush path (if we have a param) or by toggling the coalescing flag locally? If toggling helps, we can offer a customer workaround (switch to non-streaming or enable immediate flush).

alex_nguyen: I tested toggling `stream.coalesce_window_ms` locally: set to 0 -> immediate chunk flushes, first chunk latency drops to ~60ms. Setting to 20 (default recently) -> 900-1100ms. So this points to coalescing window.

maria.perez: Customer confirmed quick test — they set `streaming=false` (non-streaming/sync) and saw the immediate UI improvement (first render appears faster even though total time similar). So we have a short-term mitigation. :white_check_mark:

jonathan.kirby: Long term fix options: 1) revert PR and re-evaluate (heavy), 2) reduce coalescing window and add heuristics (e.g., if first chunk size < X, always flush), 3) expose a per-tenant override for coalescing. My preference: tighten heuristics (option 2) and add a canary rollout.

liz_sre: Also we should add an SLI for "first_chunk_latency" (TTFB for streaming) and alert when p95 > 500ms for >5m. Right now we only have total response time metrics. I'll create an Ops ticket.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1034 — streaming first-chunk latency regression. Assigned: liz_sre, jonathan.kirby.

deploybot: Rolled back runtime r-2026-03-11-coalesce -> r-2026-03-09-stable in us-east-1 at 2026-03-12T03:10:44Z for affected pods (canary then manual). Rolling rollback to other regions in progress.

maria.perez: Customer verified after rollback that streaming TTFB returned to baseline (~60-80ms). They appreciate the rollback. :pray: We'll keep them updated on a permanent fix.

jonathan.kirby: Action items I will own: 1) implement heuristic: do not coalesce the first chunk or if chunk_size < 512 bytes; 2) add feature flag `stream.coalesce_first_chunk=false` default false for canary; 3) instrument first_chunk_latency metric. Target PR by EOD tomorrow.

liz_sre: I'll set up the alert and add runbook steps: immediate mitigation = rollback or set tenant to non-streaming, medium = reduce window to 5ms in canary, long = heuristic + tests.

alex_nguyen: Thanks all. I'll update the customer with the rollback result and planned timeline for a permanent fix. Closing loop here once the PR merges and we confirm metrics stable.

maria.perez: Adding notes to the support ticket with repro steps, temporary workaround (streaming=false) and link to this thread.

jonathan.kirby: FYI, added a unit + integration test that asserts chunk is flushed within X ms for small responses. Will run in CI.

liz_sre: Follow-up: created alert rule A-STREAM-TTFB-01 and Ops runbook doc link: https://internal/docs/ops/streaming-ttfb. Assigning to oncall for 72h watch.

alex_nguyen: Great, thanks. Marking resolved for now pending PR merge. :thumbsup:
